title: Employees at AT&T fiber subsidiary could strike if contract agreement isn't reached
html:
Workers at Forged Fiber 37, a subsidiary of US telecoms giant AT&T, could go on strike as employees at the company push for improved contracts.

Communications Workers of America (CWA), which represents communications workers across the US, including employees at Forged Fiber 37, said that workers at the fiber joint venture have "overwhelmingly voted to authorize a strike if necessary."

Workers at the company are battling for a fair first contract with AT&T, according to the CWA.

Forged Fiber 37 has more than 1,300 employees across the US. Employees at the company install, maintain, and support the fiber network that AT&T is growing across the country.

CWA said the vote follows months of negotiations with AT&T, with the worker's union critical of the carrier's "approach to bargaining."

The union notes that AT&T withdrew a tentative agreement that had been reached with the union, leading the CWA to file an unfair labor practice charge with the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) over the company's actions.

Talks began back in May, with employees seeking basic protections that should come with a fair contract, including job security, reasonable time off, and wages and benefits that reflect the value of their work.

But the union accuses AT&T of laying off union employees and opting for contractors and temporary workers, even when trained and qualified union members are available to do the work.

“As a union technician, I take immense pride in building high-quality fiber networks that connect my community,” said Richard Castillo, Fiber Tech II, CWA Local 7704 Utah. “I’ve seen the shoddy, and even dangerous, work done by contractors with no ties to the community. Together, Forged Fiber workers are taking a stand for quality service by local union workers that our communities deserve. We’re ready to do what it takes to get a fair contract.”

The timing of the CWA's threat of strike action comes a month after AT&T, along with BlackRock subsidiary Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPP Investments), combined Forged Fiber 37 and Gigapower under one wholesale fiber commercial open access company. The combination was part of plans to speed up AT&T's fiber rollout across the US.

The CWA has previously been critical of Gigapower, accusing the company of building its fiber network through a network of subcontractors with little direct employment of technicians.

"The workers who build, maintain, and keep its fiber network running are the same workers whose labor AT&T depends on while trying to strip away the job security they deserve," said Susie McAllister, vice president, CWA District 7.

"Our members have drawn a line: job security and reliable service our communities depend on are not negotiable, and neither is a fair contract. If AT&T refuses to do what’s right, we will be ready to take our labor off the job at a day and time of our choosing. They should not underestimate the power of workers who are ready to do what it takes for the fair contract they deserve."

Forged Fiber 37 employees will continue to report to work under the current terms and conditions while negotiations continue.

"The strike authorization gives CWA President Claude Cummings Jr. the authority to call a strike if necessary, as the union continues to push AT&T to reach a fair agreement," added the CWA.

“Forged Fiber 37 is committed to working with the Communications Workers of America (CWA) to reach a fair agreement that recognizes employees’ role in delivering outstanding service to customers," said an AT&T spokesperson in a statement to DCD.

AT&T previously clashed with the CWA in 2024 when more than 17,000 AT&T workers across nine Southeastern US states took industrial action against the carrier over a contract dispute. Those strikes lasted for 30 days, the longest in history at the carrier, before an agreement was reached.
summary: The CWA confirms workers at Forged Fiber 37 have "overwhelmingly voted to authorize a strike if necessary"
